 -2-  MFA No. 2404 of 2015 BANGALORE, DISMISSING THE APPLICATION FILED U/SEC 16 OF THE RAILWAY CLAIMS TRIBUNAL ACT, 1987 R/W SEC 124-A OF RAILWAYS ACT, 1989.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 23(1) of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') has been filed by the applicants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 17.12.2014 passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Bangalore Bench (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') in O.A.II U 146/2010 whereby the application is dismissed.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 30.03.2019 around 6.00 a.m. Smt.Rukkamma, w/o. late Ramaswsamy has boarded the train in Mysuru to go to Nanjanagudu after purchasing the valid train ticket.

Since the train was over- crowded, the deceased was forced to stand near the door and the train started with a big jerk and jolt, due to which the deceased lost her balance and accidentally fell down from the moving train at Mysuru railways station, suffered injuries and immediately, she was shifted to the hospital where she succumbed to the injuries.
The applicants are the children of the deceased.
They filed the original application under Section 16 of the Act before the Tribunal in O.A.No.146/2010.
3. To prove their case, the first applicant examined himself as AW1 and produced Exs.A1 to A9.
The respondent has not examined any witness but produced DRM Investigation Report as Ex.R1.
On the basis of the evidence of the parties, the Tribunal has dismissed the application.
Being aggrieved by the same, the applicant is before this Court.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants has raised the following contentions:
Firstly, the first applicant himself was examined as AW-1.
He has categorically stated that the deceased, after purchasing the ticket has boarded the train on 30.03.2019 from Mysuru to Nanjanagudu town.

Due to heavy rush, she lost balance, fell down,
suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

Immediately thereafter, the police complaint has been lodged and after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet and also final report stating that the deceased died when she was traveling in the R Venkatesh vs Union Of India on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12494835/
2 train, she lost balance, fell down and suffered injuries.

sentences.text: The applicant has examined himself as AW-1 and has discharged his burden to prove that the deceased was a bonafide passenger, fell down from the moving train, suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
To disprove the case of the applicant, respondent has not examined any witnesses.
The Tribunal has erred in dismissing the claim petition holding that the applicant has not proved his case.
In support of his contentious, he has relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of UNION OF INDIA vs. RINA DEVI reported in (2019) 3 SCC 572.

entities.text: UNION OF INDIA vs. RINA DEVI reported in (2019) 3 SCC 572
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent has contended that the deceased was not a bonafide passenger and the ticket was not recovered from the body of the deceased and the applicant has failed to prove that the deceased was travelling in the train and she fell down from the train.
He further contended that even there is a contradictory evidence.

As per the post-mortem report,
death was caused due to the injury to head which may be due to railway accident.
Therefore, she has not suffered any injury and succumbed to the injury by falling from the train and the Tribunal has rightly rejected the application.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned order and the original records.
7.
The case of the applicants is that on 30.03.2019 around 6.00 a.m. Smt.Rukkamma, w/o. late Ramaswsamy has boarded the train in Mysuru to go to Nanjanagudu after purchasing the valid train ticket.

Since the train was over- crowded the deceased was forced to stand near the door and the train started with a big jerk and jolt, due to which the deceased lost her balance and accidentally fell down from the moving train at Mysuru railways station, suffered injuries and immediately she was shifted to the hospital where she succumbed to the injuries.
To prove their case, first applicant was examined as AW-1.

He has categorically stated that the deceased boarded the train in Mysuru railway station after purchasing the ticket, she fell down and suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
In the DMA report produced by the respondent, it has been stated that the deceased might have fell down from the train and thereby might have caused the accident resulting in her death.
Even, the police, after thorough investigation have filed the final report stating that the deceased was traveling in the train, she fell down, suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
By examining AW1 and producing the documents, the applicants have discharged their initial burden and now the burden has been shifted to the railways.
It has not examined any witnesses and has not discharged its burden.

In fact, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of RINA DEVI (supra) has held as follows:
" 25.

We are unable to uphold the above view as the concept of 'self-inflicted injury'
would require intention to inflict such injury and not mere negligence of any particular degree.

Doing so would amount to invoking the R Venkatesh vs Union Of India on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12494835/
3  principle of contributory negligence which cannot be done in the case of liability based on 'no fault theory'.

sentences.text: We may in this connection refer to judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. versus Sunil Kumar [(2019) 12 SCC 398 laying down that plea of negligence of the victim cannot be allowed in claim based on 'no fault theory' under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. versus Sunil Kumar [(2019) 12 SCC 398
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we hold that death or injury in the course of boarding or de-boarding a train will be an 'untoward incident' entitling a victim to the compensation and will not fall under the proviso to Section 124-A merely on the plea of negligence of the victim as a contributing factor.

Re: (iii) Burden of Proof When Body Found on Railway Premises - Definition of Passenger :
26.
Conflict of decisions has been pointed out on the subject.
As noticed from the statutory provision, compensation is payable for death or injury of a 'passenger'.

In Raj Kumari (supra) referring to the scheme of Railways Act, 1890, it was observed that since travelling without ticket was punishable, the burden was on the railway administration to prove that passenger was not a bonafide passenger.
The Railway Administration has special knowledge whether ticket was issued or not.
The 1989 Act also has similar provisions being Sections 55 and 137.
This view has led to an inference that any person dead or injured found on the railway premises has to be presumed to be a bona fide passenger so as to maintain a claim for compensation.
However, Delhi High Court in Gurcharan Singh (supra) held that initial onus to prove death or injury to a bona fide passenger is always on the claimant.
However, such onus can shift on Railways if an affidavit of relevant facts is filed by the claimant.
A negative onus cannot be placed on the Railways.

Onus to prove that the deceased or injured was a bona fide passenger can be discharged even in absence of a ticket if relevant facts are shown that ticket was purchased but it was lost."
8.
In view of the above, it is very clear that the respondent / railways failed to discharge its burden or disprove the case of the applicants.
Under these circumstances, the Tribunal has erred in dismissing the application.
9. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The judgment dated 17.12.2014 in OA No.146/2010 passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Bangalore Bench is set aside.

The matter is remitted back to the Tribunal with a direction to re-consider the matter afresh in accordance with law keeping in view the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of RINA DEVI (supra) and without being influenced by the observations made in this order.
